Let $t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ and $\mathcal{I}_{U_{\infty}}$ the standard Harish-Chandra sheaf for $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ attached to the open $N$ -orbit $U_{\infty}\subset X$ . Then as $\mathfrak{g}$ -modules,

$\Gamma(X,\mathcal{I}_{U_{\infty}})\simeq I(t-1),$

where $I(t-1)$ is the dual Verma module of highest weight $t-1$ .

7. Admissible representations of $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$

In Section 6, we described the $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ -modules corresponding to Verma modules and dual Verma modules. These $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ -modules were the standard Harish-Chandra sheaves for the Harish-Chandra pair $(\mathfrak{g},N)$ . In this section, we will describe four $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ -modules which are constructed in a similar way from $K$ -orbits on $X$ , where

$K=\left\{\left.\begin{pmatrix}a&0\\
0&a^{-1}\end{pmatrix}\right|a\in\mathbb{C}^{\times}\right\}.$

These are the standard Harish-Chandra sheaves for the Harish-Chandra pair ( $\mathfrak{g},K)$ . The group $K$ is the complexification of the maximal compact subgroup of the real Lie group

$\SU(1,1)=\left\{M\in\SL(2,\mathbb{C})\left|M\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\
0&-1\end{pmatrix}M^{*}=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\
0&-1\end{pmatrix}\right.\right\},$

which is isomorphic to $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ . We will see that the global sections of the standard Harish-Chandra sheaves described in this section are the Harish-Chandra modules attached to discrete series and principal series representations of $\SL(2,\mathbb{R})$ .

The group $K$ acts on $X$ by restriction of the action (2.2). There are three orbits: the two single-point orbits $0$ and $\infty$ , and the open orbit $V\simeq\mathbb{C}^{\times}$ .
$=$ $\sqcup$ $0$ $X$ $V$ $\sqcup$ $\infty$

We will begin by describing the standard Harish-Chandra sheaves constructed from the closed orbits. The standard Harish-Chandra sheaf associated to the orbit $0$ is

$\mathcal{I}_{0}:=i_{0+}(\mathcal{O}_{0}).$

We described the structure of this $\mathcal{D}_{t}$ -module in Section 6. The $\mathfrak{g}$ -module structure on its space of global sections is given by formulas (6.3) - (6.5) and Figure 2.

The standard Harish-Chandra sheaf

$\mathcal{I}_{\infty}:=i_{\infty+}(\mathcal{O}_{\infty})$

attached to the closed orbit $\infty$ has a similar structure. As it is supported entirely in the chart $U_{\infty}$ , it suffices to describe only $\mathcal{I}_{\infty}(U_{\infty})$ . By analogous arguments to those in Section 6, we have

$\mathcal{I}_{\infty}(U_{\infty})=\bigoplus_{i\geq 0}\partial_{w}^{i}\delta,$

where $\delta$ is the Dirac indicator function. The actions of $E_{\infty},F_{\infty}$ , and $H_{\infty}$ on the basis

$\left\{d_{k}:=\frac{(-1)^{k}}{k!}\partial_{w}^{k}\delta\right\}_{k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}}$

are given by the formulas

(7.1)

$\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{1,0,0}E_{\infty}}\cdot d_{k}$
$\displaystyle=(k+1)d_{k+1},$

(7.2)

$\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}F_{\infty}}\cdot d_{k}$
$\displaystyle=(-t-k)d_{k-1}\text{ for }k>0,\hskip 5.69054pt{\color[rgb]{0,0,1}F_{\infty}}\cdot d_{0}=0,$

(7.3)

$\displaystyle{\color[rgb]{0,1,1}H_{\infty}}\cdot d_{k}$
$\displaystyle=(t+1+2k)d_{k}.$

Figure 5 illustrates this $\mathfrak{g}$ -module structure. We can see that for $t\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$ , $\Gamma(X,\mathcal{I}_{\infty})$ is an irreducible lowest weight module with lowest weight $t+1$ .
card.label: Theorem 6.3

paper.title: Four examples of Beilinson-Bernstein localization
paper.abstract: Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a complex semisimple Lie algebra. The Beilinson-Bernstein localization theorem establishes an equivalence of the category of $\mathfrak{g}$-modules of a fixed infinitesimal character and a category of modules over a twisted sheaf of differential operators on the flag variety of $\mathfrak{g}$. In this expository paper, we give four detailed examples of this theorem when $\mathfrak{g}=\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb{C})$. Specifically, we describe the $\mathcal{D}$-modules associated to finite-dimensional irreducible $\mathfrak{g}$-modules, Verma modules, Whittaker modules, discrete series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$, and principal series representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{R})$.
